title: app-shell: a `type: 'flow'` action's button starts its flow through `POST /automation/:name/trigger`, not the action door — decide whether the button routes through `POST /actions/:object/:action` so the action's own server-side gates apply
body:
Filing gate: ③ — a task the maintainer's ruling assigns: objectstack-ai/objectstack#22407 ruling A (`6074046403`, maintainer 「同意」 2026-10-09T04:05Z).
Reader: objectui triage (routing and grading), then the execution seat of the lane it routes to. This card asks for a lane decision; it is not a dispatch order.
Dedupe: two semantic searches of objectstack-ai/objectui (flow action button, trigger route, action door, `requiredPermissions`, 403 elevated flow) returned 6 hits, all closed and none on this question (#11779, #2958, #9973, #7234, #4421; #2958 twice). One search of objectstack-ai/objectstack returned 15 hits; the only related ones are objectstack-ai/objectstack#22407 and objectstack-ai/objectstack#22310, the parent rulings.

## The ruling's words (quoted, not translated)

> The console's flow-action button route is not part of this ruling: under A both doors answer alike, and whether objectui routes the button through the action door so the action's own gates apply is a UI card after landing.

Ruling A landed in objectstack-ai/objectstack#22424 (merge commit `c572fe2a36`, 2026-10-09T07:11Z), which closes objectstack-ai/objectstack#22407. Every door that starts a flow by name — the trigger route, a `type: 'flow'` action (REST and MCP `run_action`) and a declared `type: 'flow'` endpoint — now refuses a non-system caller a flow declared `runAs: 'system'` whose type is `autolaunched`, `record_change` or `schedule` (`403 PERMISSION_DENIED`, nothing runs).

## What the console does today (read at objectui `origin/main` `8f815f4f`)

Both flow-action handlers call the trigger route with the action's `target`. Neither calls the action door:
- `packages/app-shell/src/hooks/useConsoleActionRuntime.tsx:589–624` (`flowHandler`): `POST ${baseUrl}/api/v1/automation/${flowName}/trigger`.
- `packages/app-shell/src/views/RecordDetailView.tsx:1118–1140` (`flowHandler`): the same route.

The action door, `POST /api/v1/actions/:object/:action` (`dispatchFlowAction` in `@objectstack/runtime`), answers more than the trigger route does for the same click:
- the action's declared `requiredPermissions`, enforced on the server (ADR-0066 D4: a dual-surface gate whose UI half only hides the button);
- the caller-scoped subject-record load and its `recordLoadDenied` verdict.

On the trigger route, none of these runs. Under ruling A, the elevated-start refusal now answers alike at both doors. These other gates still differ.

## The question for the lane

Should the console's flow-action buttons call the action door, so that each server-side gate the action declares applies to the click? Or does the trigger route stay, with the reason recorded?

Measure before deciding:
- whether the action door's response shape (the ADR-0112 envelope, a paused screen run's resume handle) carries everything both handlers read today, including FlowRunner's resume and the refused-end toast;
- how the action door identifies the action for related-list row actions that retarget the flow at a child record.
